meta.source_title: Ministry of Home Affairs — Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
meta.notice: BNS applies subject to the date of the alleged offence and the savings clause. Older incidents may continue under IPC.

murder.punishment: Death or imprisonment for life, and fine
consequences: Trial is ordinarily before a Court of Session.
A fine may be imposed in addition to imprisonment.
Group murder on specified identity grounds is separately covered by Section 103(2).

attempt to murder.punishment: Up to 10 years and fine; if hurt is caused, imprisonment for life may apply
consequences: The result depends heavily on intention, knowledge and the surrounding circumstances.
Causing hurt can increase exposure up to imprisonment for life.
Weapon use and medical evidence may materially affect the charge.

culpable homicide.punishment: Life imprisonment or 5–10 years and fine where intention is proved; up to 10 years and fine where there is knowledge without intention
consequences: The applicable range changes depending on intention versus knowledge.
A fine may be imposed with imprisonment.
Medical and forensic evidence is central to distinguishing this offence from murder.

hurt.punishment: Up to 1 year, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both
consequences: The injury report may determine whether the allegation is simple or grievous hurt.
A fine can be imposed instead of or together with imprisonment.
Special circumstances or use of dangerous means can attract other sections.

grievous hurt.punishment: Up to 7 years and fine; aggravated forms may attract higher punishment
consequences: Fracture, dislocation, permanent impairment and specified serious injuries may qualify.
Dangerous weapons or means can attract Section 118 and higher punishment.
Medical evidence determines the nature and severity of injury.
Kidnapping from India and from lawful guardianship are covered.
Ransom, murder, begging or exploitation purposes can attract much higher punishment.
Age, consent and lawful guardianship are important facts.

abduction.punishment: No single general punishment; the purpose and connected offence determine the penalty
consequences: Force or deceitful inducement is part of the definition.
Abduction for murder, ransom, grievous hurt or exploitation attracts separate provisions.
The purpose of taking the person is essential to the final charge.

rape.punishment: Rigorous imprisonment of at least 10 years, extendable to life, and fine; aggravated cases may carry higher punishment
consequences: The court may direct that the fine support the victim's medical and rehabilitation needs where provided by law.
Aggravated circumstances and the victim's age can materially increase punishment.
Consent, age and medical or digital evidence require careful legal assessment.

sexual harassment.punishment: Up to 3 years, or fine, or both for specified physical advances, demands or pornography; up to 1 year, or fine, or both for sexually coloured remarks
consequences: The punishment differs according to the exact act alleged.
Workplace incidents may also trigger proceedings under the POSH Act and employer policy.
Messages, recordings and witness accounts may become important evidence.

stalking.punishment: Up to 3 years and fine for a first conviction; up to 5 years and fine for a subsequent conviction
consequences: Repeated unwanted contact and monitoring of electronic communication are covered.
A subsequent conviction carries a higher maximum sentence.
Call records, messages and platform evidence may be relevant.

dowry death.punishment: At least 7 years, extendable to imprisonment for life
consequences: The provision addresses specified unnatural deaths within seven years of marriage.
Evidence of dowry-related cruelty or harassment soon before death is important.
Related cruelty and Dowry Prohibition Act offences may also be investigated.

theft.punishment: Up to 3 years, or fine, or both; repeat conviction can lead to 1–5 years rigorous imprisonment and fine
consequences: For a first conviction involving property below ₹5,000, restoration can result in community service under the statutory proviso.
Repeat convictions carry a higher minimum and maximum term.
Theft from a dwelling, transport, place of worship or government property can attract Section 305 and up to 7 years plus fine.

robbery.punishment: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years and fine; highway robbery between sunset and sunrise may extend to 14 years
consequences: Attempted robbery can attract up to 7 years and fine.
Causing hurt during robbery can expose participants to life imprisonment or up to 10 years rigorous imprisonment and fine.
Use of a deadly weapon can attract additional or enhanced provisions.

dacoity.punishment: Imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine
consequences: Dacoity involves five or more persons committing, attempting or aiding robbery.
Murder during dacoity can expose every participant to death, life imprisonment or at least 10 years rigorous imprisonment and fine.
Preparation, assembly and membership of a habitual dacoity gang are separately punishable.

cheating.punishment: Up to 3 years, or fine, or both; cheating that dishonestly induces delivery of property may extend to 7 years and fine
consequences: A broken promise alone is not automatically cheating; dishonest intention at the relevant time matters.
Property-delivery and valuable-security cases carry a higher maximum sentence.
Banking records, communications and transaction trails may be examined.

criminal breach of trust.punishment: Up to 5 years, or fine, or both; specified occupations and public servants can face higher punishment
consequences: Entrustment and dishonest misuse are central elements.
Carriers, warehouse-keepers, clerks and servants can face up to 7 years and fine.
Public servants, bankers, merchants, brokers, attorneys or agents can face life imprisonment or up to 10 years and fine.

forgery.punishment: Up to 2 years, or fine, or both; forgery intended for cheating may extend to 7 years and fine
consequences: False electronic records are expressly covered.
Forgery for cheating carries a higher maximum sentence.
Use of forged court, public, identity or valuable-security documents may attract separate aggravated provisions.

defamation.punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both, or community service
consequences: BNS retains statutory exceptions, including specified good-faith statements.
Community service is an available sentencing option.
Printing, engraving or selling defamatory matter can be separately punishable.

rioting.punishment: Up to 2 years, or fine, or both; armed rioting may extend to 5 years, or fine, or both
consequences: Every member using force or violence for the common object can be liable for rioting.
Being armed with a deadly weapon increases the maximum sentence.
Members may also be liable for offences committed in prosecution of the common object under Section 190.

unlawful assembly.punishment: Membership may attract up to 6 months, or fine, or both; continuing after a lawful dispersal command may attract up to 2 years, or fine, or both
consequences: An assembly generally requires five or more persons and a prohibited common object.
Knowing continuation after a lawful order to disperse increases exposure.
Armed participation and offences committed for the common object may attract additional liability.

public nuisance.punishment: The applicable punishment depends on the specific nuisance provision, continuing conduct and any local law involved
consequences: A public nuisance must affect the public or people in the vicinity, not merely one private dispute.
Continuing a nuisance after a lawful direction can lead to additional consequences.
Municipal, traffic, environmental or noise-control laws may also apply.

acid attack.punishment: For causing specified acid injuries: 10 years to life and fine; attempt: 5–7 years and fine
consequences: The fine must be just and reasonable to meet the victim's medical expenses and is payable to the victim.
Attempting to throw or administer acid is separately punishable even when the intended injury is not completed.
Medical evidence and proof of intention or knowledge are central.

human trafficking.punishment: Generally 7–10 years rigorous imprisonment and fine; multiple victims, children, repeat offences or public-servant involvement can lead to 10 years to life
consequences: The victim's consent is immaterial to determining trafficking under the section.
Trafficking of children or multiple persons carries enhanced minimum punishment.
Repeat child trafficking or involvement of a public servant or police officer can result in imprisonment for the remainder of natural life and fine.
